review.reason: 리뷰 거절: server/internal/figures/figures.go:73 `case character == ',' || unicode.IsSpace(character)` no longer ends the figure at a space, so a value holding several numbers glues them together. The documented line-chart row form (docs/deck-source.md:91 `- 전환 전 | 120, 118, 121, 119`) is parsed by parseSourceItem -> figures.Of into 1.20118121119e+11 instead of 120. Verified by running the same probe on both trees: main gives Number=120 for that row, HEAD gives Number=1.20118121119e+11. / server/internal/deck/source.go:700 the regression above escapes to user-visible output. compile.go leaves Items on a ::line block (only ::table clears them, compile.go:143), pptx.SanitizeBlock keeps them, and inspect.go:752 includes BlockLine in plottedFigures. statesFigure("120, 118, 121, 119") is false, so the audit emits the finding `figures with no source: 전환 전 120118121119` (verified by direct call to plottedFigures). Before this change it read `전환 전 120`. No test covers this path.

notes: server/internal/figures/figures_test.go:74 TestAloneAndOfReadTheSameFigure cannot fail: Alone and Of are both thin wrappers over the same read(), so the invariant holds by construction, not by test. It guards nothing today and would keep passing if the two ever diverged in the wrappers only.

The CSV/spreadsheet part of the change is genuinely verified. I copied sheetamounts_test.go onto a worktree at main: 4/6 subtests of TestASheetOfMoneyIsDrawnAsAChart and 5/5 of TestTheChartReadsTheFiguresTheSheetWasSentOnFor fail there and pass on HEAD, and the two 'still a table' subtests are deliberate regression guards. The whole suite (go test ./...) passes on HEAD.

server/internal/docs/tables.go:254 is slightly stricter than the old strconv.ParseFloat check in one direction: a column written in scientific notation ("1e5") used to be charted and is now laid out as a table. It is also stricter about "NaN"/"Inf", which ParseFloat accepted and which used to produce a chart with unusable heights — that direction is an improvement.

The commit message says "there is one reading now", but server/internal/deck/compile.go:1406 parseBareNumber is a third, independent reading of the same kind of value (used for ::line series points) and was left untouched. Not a defect by itself, but the claim overstates what the diff does.

"(340)" now makes a column chartable and is drawn by magnitude (pptx/blocks.go:1240, :1293 use math.Abs), so a refund draws the same direction and size as revenue of +340. The commit message acknowledges this; the value label still shows "(340)". Flagging as a design consequence, not a defect.
Nothing here touches auth, payments, migrations, workflows, secrets or deletion; the change is pure parsing with no external state, so it reverts cleanly with a plain git revert.
